To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electrochemical properties of the composite particles are dependent on the method of synthesis and the nature of the organic and inorganic components.
the double-strand polynaniline in the composite show better pH stability of conductive form than the corresponding single-stranded polyaniline in core/shell composites.
we have synthesized new inorganic/ organic composite particles with a double-strand conducting polymer shell, which show electronic interaction between their organic and inorganic components.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and properties of new organic/inorganic composite particles with core/shell structure and with the development of a novel electrochemical method for their synthesis.
the synthesis of new composite materials and the characterization of their electronic and optical properties.
the development of new inorganic materials for the synthesis of new materials with improved properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the synthesis of the composite particles is feasible by using three different methods, and that the electrochemical behavior of the composite particles depends on the method of synthesis.
the double-strand polynaniline shell is more effective in improving the stability of the conducting form of polyaniline.
the double-strand polypyrrole/polyaniline shell in the core/shell composite particles has a higher conductivity and a more stable pH response than the corresponding single-stranded polyaniline.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the organic/inorganic interface is an important feature of the composite particles, and the electronic interaction between the inorganic and organic components is a key factor to determine the properties of the composite particles.

a double-strand organic polymer shell can be synthesized in the core/shell composite, and this double-strand organic shell has better electronic and pH stability than the single-strand organic shell in the core/shall composite.
the double-strand polyelectrolyte shell in the composite materials is more stable than the single strand polyelectroliytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use a double-strand conducting polymer to stabilize a core/shell composite material.
the electronic properties of the organic shell can be modified by the choice of inorganic core.
the inorganic/organic interface can be controlled by the choice of the core material, shell material, and the method of synthesis.
